statements.impact_statement: The flaw is in util-linux's mount(8)/nsenter(1) programs. The image carries only the libuuid1 shared library from util-linux, not those programs (distroless: no mount, no nsenter, no setuid binaries).

The overflow is in the infocmp command-line program (progs/infocmp.c). The image carries only the libtinfo6/libncursesw6 shared libraries, not infocmp.

Only tarfile's extraction filters are affected. No code in the image extracts a tar archive: the service's own packages do not import tarfile, and the dependencies that do only write archives (dulwich) or read members of their own bundled data (dateutil.zoneinfo).

Only html.parser.HTMLParser is affected. The web service parses HTML from its own static directory (the viewer and campaign browser) to hash inline scripts for Content-Security-Policy. The converter image does not use html.parser. botocore imports html.parser only in botocore/docs/bcdoc/docstringparser.py on its own bundled service-model documentation, never on network input.

The web image's results proxy parses S3 store XML responses using botocore's XML parser (xml.etree.ElementTree → libexpat). Store access is HTTPS but S3_VERIFY_TLS may be false. Keep TLS verification on where the store certificate can be verified. Upgrade to fixed libpython3.13 packages when released.
statements.action_statement: The web image parses S3 store's XML responses with expat. Keep S3 TLS verification enabled. Upgrade to fixed Debian libpython3.13 packages when released; libexpat1 fixes follow. The converter image does not parse XML and is unaffected.
